title: Getting Started with Python
summary: What Python is and what a variable is, in plain language, before any syntax.

checkpoints.title: What is Python?
checkpoints.content: Python is a programming language: you write step-by-step instructions called code, and the computer runs them in order, one line at a time. Every lesson here lets you write and run real code yourself, right in the browser — no installation needed.
checkpoints.explanation: You don't need to memorize anything yet — you'll see real code and run it starting in the next lesson.

hints.H0: Think of code as a recipe: a list of steps the computer follows in order.
hints.H1: You'll type real Python and immediately see what it does — that's how every lesson works.
hints.H2: No setup needed — just click Continue when you're ready to see your first example.

checkpoints.title: What is a variable?
checkpoints.content: A variable is a named box that holds a value. Writing `age = 7` creates a box named `age` and puts 7 inside it. Later, whenever your code uses `age`, Python looks inside that box to find 7.
checkpoints.explanation: Names make code easier to read and change — you update the box's contents in one place instead of everywhere that value is used.

hints.H0: The `=` sign doesn't mean "equals" like in math — it means "store this value under this name."
hints.H1: `age = 7` reads as: put the value 7 into a box named age.
hints.H2: If you later write `age = 8`, the same box now holds 8 instead.

checkpoints.title: Check your understanding

options.text: A fixed value that can never change.
options.explanation: Variables can be reassigned — writing `age = 8` later would change what's inside the box.

options.text: A name that currently points to the value 7.
options.explanation: Exactly — `age` is a name pointing at a value, and it can point at a different value later.

options.text: A math equation Python needs to solve.
options.explanation: There's nothing to solve here — it's an instruction to store a value under a name, not an equation.

checkpoints.explanation: A variable is just a name attached to a value, and that name can be pointed at a new value at any time.

hints.H0: Re-read the box analogy from the previous note.
hints.H1: The name `age` isn't the number itself — it's a label on a box containing the number.
hints.H2: The correct answer describes a name pointing at a value, not the value itself being fixed.
